items.title: [AI리더의 서가] AI는 어떻게 기업의 무기가 되는가
items.summary: AI는 어떻게 기업의 무기가 되는가이지성 | 처음북스2026년 10월 1일추천이유저자는 PwC 컨설턴트로서 15년간의 현장 경험을 바탕으로 AI 도입 후에도 업무가 개선되지 않는 이유를 진단하고, 회사의 기존 지식과 프로세스를 AI의 실력으로 변환하는 구체적인 방법을 제시합니다. 독자는 첫 90일의 실행 전략부터 5개 부서의 실제 적용 사례, 조직 변화 관리까지 체계적으로 학습하며 회사에 맞는 AI 에이전트 운영 체계를 구축할 수 있습니다.상세보기 AI를 도입했는데 일이 줄지 않는 회사가 많다.
items.content:
저자는 PwC 컨설턴트로서 15년간의 현장 경험을 바탕으로 AI 도입 후에도 업무가 개선되지 않는 이유를 진단하고, 회사의 기존 지식과 프로세스를 AI의 실력으로 변환하는 구체적인 방법을 제시합니다. 독자는 첫 90일의 실행 전략부터 5개 부서의 실제 적용 사례, 조직 변화 관리까지 체계적으로 학습하며 회사에 맞는 AI 에이전트 운영 체계를 구축할 수 있습니다.

AI를 도입했는데 일이 줄지 않는 회사가 많다. 프로그램 설치는 보안 정책에 걸리고, 필요한 데이터에는 권한이 없고, 자동으로 만든 보고서는 다시 엑셀로 옮겨 적는다.

영풍문고 북마스터는 이 익숙한 막막함에서 출발하는 책으로 처음북스가 지난 10월 1일 펴낸 『 AI는 어떻게 기업의 무기가 되는가 』를 골랐다. 저자 이지성은 PwC 컨설팅의 AI·데이터·AX 컨설턴트이자 정보관리기술사로, 15년 동안 금융·제조·엔지니어링 현장의 AI 프로젝트를 맡아 왔다.

영풍문고 MD들이 가장 먼저 밑줄을 친 곳은 유통사의 문서 창고 사례다. 책은 이렇게 쓴다. "회사는 거대한 문서 창고를 만드는 데는 성공했다. 그러나 창고가 커질수록 어떤 문서를 믿어야 하는지는 더욱 불분명해졌다. (…) 기록이 존재한다는 것과 조직이 그 내용을 공식적인 지식으로 합의했다는 것은 전혀 다른 문제라는 점이다."

권기원 영풍문고 서적팀 팀장은 "사내 RAG 챗봇이 엉뚱한 답을 내는 이유를 기술이 아니라 조직의 합의에서 찾는 대목"이라며 "AX를 맡은 실무자라면 이 한 문단으로 회의 방향이 달라질 것"이라고 말했다.

비슷한 주제의 책과 견주면 이 책의 자리가 더 분명해진다. 『 실전 AX 리포트 』가 한 대기업 AX 팀이 52개 계열사로 AI를 넓혀 간 확산기라면, 『 인간과 봇이 협력하는 AX경영 』은 경영학자의 시선으로 인간과 봇의 '증강'을 다룬 조직론이다. 『 AI를 어떻게 통제할 것인가 』는 내부통제와 감사의 언어로 거버넌스를 설계한다. 이 책은 그 사이에서 첫 90일을 어떻게 보낼지를 묻는다. 업무를 네 가지 유형으로 나누고, 첫 과제를 고르는 다섯 가지 원칙을 세우고, 부서 간 용어와 승인 구조, 보안 통제를 '하네스 매핑'으로 정리한다.

이원준 영풍문고 기술부문 MD는 "인사·마케팅·영업·운영·재무 다섯 부서의 적용 사례가 있어 기술팀과 현업이 같은 그림을 보고 이야기할 수 있다"고 평가했다.

후반부는 도입 이후를 다룬다. 익숙한 업무 화면에 자동화를 녹이는 '보이지 않는 자동화', 두려움에서 호기심을 거쳐 의존으로 이어지는 변화 관리 3단계, 중간관리자의 KPI를 다시 짜는 방법을 설명한다. 1년 실행 로드맵과 성숙도 자가진단으로 마무리하면서, 사람을 줄이지 않는 AI 프로젝트가 투자 효과를 무엇으로 증명할지까지 따진다.

-『 AI는 어떻게 기업의 무기가 되는가 』

- 처음북스 | 2026년 10월 1일 출간 | 272쪽 | 정가 21,000원

- ISBN 9791170223351

영풍문고는 1992년 종로에서 문을 연 이래 34년간 책과 독자를 이어온 서점입니다. 현재 전국 46개 지점과 온라인몰 을 운영하며, 100만명의 회원에게 도서와 문화 콘텐츠를 제공하고 있습니다.

items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.summary: The affair could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
items.content:
Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security.

United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, the Times has reported.

The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang , and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per the Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed .

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

items.title: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
items.summary: As soon as Wednesday evening, Nvidia's board could decide to remove its founder and CEO of 33 years.
items.content:
Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years, the Wall Street Journal reports . Sources told the newspaper that the Nvidia board is meeting as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future at the company.

On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman purported by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. On Wednesday evening, the New York Times reported that Huang also had an affair with an executive who reports to him.

Nvidia has become one of the most valuable companies in the world as it designs the chips that power the AI boom, but in the midst of Huang’s ongoing scandal , Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday. The stock is down about 11% in the past five days.

Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company also has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. According to Bloomberg, Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify candidates that could potentially replace Huang as CEO.

items.content:
부채 부담과 AI 투자 거품 논란으로 급락했던 미국 AI 기술주가 코어위브의 실적 발표를 계기로 일제히 반등했다. 코어위브가 예상보다 높은 매출 성장과 자금 조달 대책을 제시하면서 시장의 불안이 누그러졌고, 젠슨 황 CEO를 둘러싼 논란으로 급락했던 엔비디아 주가도 상승세로 돌아섰다.

로이터와 블룸버그 등은 11일(현지시간) AI 클라우드 기업 코어위브의 3분기 실적 발표가 미국 기술주 반등을 이끌었다고 보도했다. 코어위브 주가는 이날 24.7% 급등했으며, 네비우스(15.4%)와 어플라이드 디지털(7.4%) 등 AI 인프라 기업들도 동반 상승했다.

엔비디아는 2.87% 올라 최근 이틀 동안의 급락세에서 벗어났다. 나스닥 종합지수와 S&P500지수는 각각 1.60%, 1.31% 상승했고, 필라델피아 반도체지수는 5.7% 급등했다.

시장의 분위기를 바꾼 것은 코어위브의 실적과 향후 전망이다. 코어위브는 10일 발표한 3분기 매출이 전년 동기보다 168% 증가한 36억6000만달러(약 4조9000억원)를 기록했다고 밝혔다. 연간 매출 전망도 기존 120억~130억달러에서 130억~133억달러로 상향했다. 확보한 고객 계약에 따른 수주잔고도 1325억달러에 달했다.

코어위브는 그동안 막대한 차입금을 동원한 데이터센터 건설로 AI 투자 거품 논란의 중심에 있었다. AI 연산 수요가 둔화하거나 GPU 임대료가 하락하면 부채를 감당하기 어려울 것이라는 지적이 이어졌다. 다른 네오클라우드 기업들의 주가가 최근 급락한 것도 이러한 불안 때문이었다.

그러나 이번 실적 발표에서는 AI 연산 수요가 여전히 강하다는 사실과 함께 부채 상환에 대한 구체적인 대책이 제시됐다. 마이클 인트레이터 코어위브 CEO는 기존 고객 계약에서 발생할 현금흐름으로 현재와 향후 부채 상환을 감당할 수 있다고 밝혔다. 또 높은 금리를 감수하면서 무담보 채권을 새로 발행할 필요가 없다고 설명했다. 회사는 2028년 상반기 조정 기준 흑자 전환도 예상했다.

자금 조달 방식도 바꾸고 있다. 코어위브는 향후 3개월 동안 약 90억달러의 고객 선불금과 예치금이 유입될 것으로 예상했다. 특히 이 가운데 30억달러 이상은 이미 구축한 데이터센터 설비에 대한 신규 계약과 관련돼 추가 장비 투자 없이 확보할 수 있는 자금이다. 고객 계약을 담보로 대출을 받는 방식도 활용해 고금리 차입에 대한 의존도를 낮출 계획이다.

인트레이터 CEO는 이날 CNBC와의 인터뷰에서 사전에 예정했던 개인 보유 주식 매각 계획도 철회했다고 밝혔다. 실적과 자금 조달 전망에 대한 자신감을 보여주는 조치로 해석된다.

월가에서도 긍정적인 평가가 나왔다. 번스타인의 매디슨 레자에이 등이 이끄는 분석팀은 코어위브가 기대할 수 있는 최상의 분기 실적을 내놓았으며, 자금 조달에 대한 우려도 상당 부분 해소했다고 평가했다.

엔비디아의 반등도 주목받았다. 엔비디아는 최근 황 CEO의 사생활 논란과 중국 정보기관 관련 의혹에 대한 조사로 이틀 동안 시가총액이 약 4300억달러 감소했다. 하지만 주요 고객이자 투자 대상인 코어위브가 AI 연산 수요의 지속적인 성장을 확인하면서 투자심리가 개선됐다. 엔비디아는 장중 5% 넘게 상승한 뒤 2.87% 오른 가격에 거래를 마쳤다.

코어위브의 실적이 AI 인프라 사업의 재무적 위험까지 해소한 것은 아니다. 회사는 3분기에 7억900만달러의 순손실을 기록했고, 이자 비용만 8억4600만달러에 달했다. 파이낸셜타임스에 따르면 코어위브는 엔비디아 GPU 등을 담보로 수십억달러 규모의 추가 대출도 추진하고 있다. 데이터센터 건설에 필요한 외부 자금 조달은 계속되는 셈이다.

번스타인도 향후 AI 연산 공급 부족이 해소되면 코어위브가 가장 먼저 큰 타격을 받을 수 있다고 경고했다. 그럼에도 이번 실적은 AI 인프라 투자에 대한 시장의 시각을 바꾸는 계기가 됐다. 과도한 차입과 수익성 문제로 기술주 급락을 촉발했던 코어위브가 실제 매출 성장과 고객 계약을 통해 사업 지속 가능성을 보여주면서 엔비디아를 비롯한 AI 기술주 전반의 반등을 이끌었다.

items.title: Jensen Huang accused of having another affair — with an Nvidia exec
items.summary: Jensen Huang, who has come under fire for admitting to an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent, has been accused of having a separate affair with an Nvidia subordinate.
items.content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is already under investigation after having admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy . Now the New York Times is reporting that Huang is also suspected of having another extramarital affair, with a direct report of his at the company — Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. Powell, like Huang, is married, the outlet says.

The Times says it was told of the alleged affair by five employees at the company. The sources said that Huang and Powell were captured on video “being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel” during a conference earlier this year.

Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles, the Times notes. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for comment.

The company’s board has initiated an investigation into Huang’s publicly admitted affair. Additionally, two House Republicans said Wednesday that Congress is gearing up to subpoena Huang over the spy allegations if he doesn’t voluntarily respond to their summons to a closed-door briefing. Late Wednesday, after the reports of the second affair were published, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Nvidia board was preparing to oust Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993.

items.content:
Nvidia’s board is set to hold urgent talks about the future of its founder Jensen Huang after revelations that he had an affair with a top executive at the company, according to people familiar with the matter.

The meeting on Wednesday comes amid a deepening scandal at the $4.2 trillion group, after Donald Trump said the FBI was investigating allegations that Huang was romantically involved with an alleged Chinese spy.

The Nvidia chief executive had a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, the chipmaker’s vice-president of healthcare, according to two people familiar with the matter. Powell, a more than 18-year veteran at Nvidia, is among the company’s more prominent public figures.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Powell could not be reached for comment.

The company’s shares dropped more than 8 percent in after-hours trading after The New York Times reported the relationship with Powell and The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board could oust Huang.

The news of the second relationship will pile pressure on Huang after he on Sunday admitted to having an affair, two days after the FT reported he was romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at an Nvidia customer.

US intelligence believes Alice Huang had also been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security spy agency.

Nvidia’s board has launched an investigation into the matter and on Tuesday said it had hired a former federal prosecutor to lead the probe. But the board on Sunday backed Huang to remain as chief executive.

Trump on Monday said the FBI was looking into the situation. Senior Republicans and Democrats have called for congressional investigations into the Nvidia boss, who has become an influential voice in the president’s circle on US AI policy and export controls.

This is a developing story.

美 연구진, 성인 119명 대상 모기 3종의 선호도 분석…피부 냄새·미생물 조합이 영향

과학 입력 :2026/11/12 08:00 수정: 2026/11/12 08:38

여럿이 함께 있어도 유독 모기에 자주 물리는 사람이 있다. 그런데 어떤 모기에게 잘 물리는 사람이라도 다른 종류의 모기에게는 별다른 관심을 받지 않을 수 있다는 연구 결과가 나왔다. 모기마다 선호하는 사람의 피부 냄새와 미생물 조합이 다르기 때문이다.

10일(현지시간) 과학 전문매체 사이언스데일리에 따르면 미국 플로리다국제대(FIU) 연구진은 사람의 피부에서 발생하는 화학물질과 미생물이 모기의 흡혈 대상 선택에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 분석했다. 연구 결과는 국제학술지 '아이사이언스(iScience)'에 발표됐다.

연구진은 성인 자원자 119명을 모집해 이집트숲모기(Aedes aegypti), 흰줄숲모기(Aedes albopictus), 열대집모기(Culex quinquefasciatus) 등 세 종류의 모기가 각각 어떤 사람에게 더 강하게 끌리는지 실험했다.

이들 모기는 뎅기열과 지카바이러스 감염증, 황열, 웨스트나일열 등 다양한 감염병을 전파할 수 있는 종이다.

실험에서는 참가자의 피부 냄새를 모기에게 노출한 뒤 얼마나 많은 모기가 해당 냄새에 반응하는지 측정했다. 모기가 사람을 실제로 물도록 한 것은 아니며, 냄새에 이끌리는 정도를 비교하는 방식으로 진행됐다.

그 결과 모기 세 종류는 서로 다른 참가자 집단을 선호하는 것으로 나타났다. 일부 참가자는 두 종류 이상의 모기에게 높은 선호도를 보였지만, 세 종류 모두에게 강하게 선호된 사람은 없었다.

연구진은 모기가 모든 사람에게 동일하게 반응하는 것이 아니라 종마다 서로 다른 화학적 신호를 이용해 흡혈 대상을 선택할 가능성이 있다고 설명했다.

이 같은 차이를 확인하기 위해 연구진은 참가자의 피부에서 발생하는 휘발성 유기화합물과 피부에 서식하는 미생물의 종류를 분석했다.

사람의 피부에서는 1000종 이상의 휘발성 화합물이 발생할 수 있다. 피부에 서식하는 세균도 이러한 냄새 성분을 만드는 데 관여한다. 개인마다 피부 미생물의 종류와 비율이 다르기 때문에 체취 역시 서로 달라질 수 있다.

분석 결과 이집트숲모기는 특정 고리형 알코올 성분이 적은 사람에게 상대적으로 더 강하게 끌렸다. 남성과 여성 사이에서도 차이가 나타났는데, 이 종은 여성보다 남성에게 약간 더 높은 선호도를 보였다.

반면 흰줄숲모기는 케톤류 화합물이 상대적으로 많이 검출되는 사람을 선호했다. 일부 식물성 향과 유사한 냄새 성분도 이 모기의 유인 반응과 관련이 있었다.

열대집모기는 또 다른 냄새 조합에 반응했다. 이집트숲모기와 마찬가지로 특정 냄새 성분이 적은 사람을 선호하는 경향이 나타났지만, 선호도와 관련된 화학물질 및 피부 미생물의 조합에는 차이가 있었다.

피부 미생물 역시 모기 종류에 따라 서로 다른 영향을 미쳤다. 특정 세균이 많이 검출되는 사람이 한 종류의 모기에게는 매력적인 대상이었지만, 다른 종류의 모기에게는 그렇지 않을 수 있다는 것이다.

연구진은 이러한 차이가 모기 종마다 사람의 냄새를 감지하고 해석하는 방식이 다르게 진화했기 때문일 가능성이 있다고 분석했다.

연구를 이끈 매슈 디제나로 플로리다국제대 신경유전학자는 사람의 체취에서 모기를 유인하거나 쫓아내는 성분을 찾아내면 모기 매개 감염병을 예방하는 새로운 전략을 개발할 수 있다고 설명했다.

특히 특정 모기 종이 선호하는 냄새 성분을 이용해 유인 장치를 만들거나, 반대로 해당 성분을 차단하는 맞춤형 기피제를 개발하는 데 활용할 수 있다는 기대다.

이번 연구는 모기에 잘 물리는 체질이 하나의 특징으로 결정되는 것이 아니라 피부에서 발생하는 다양한 화학물질과 미생물의 조합, 모기의 종류에 따라 달라질 수 있음을 보여준다.

특정 냄새 성분과 모기 선호도 사이의 연관성이 확인됐다고 해서 해당 성분이 모기의 선택을 직접적으로 결정한다고 단정할 수는 없다. 연구진이 분석한 것은 실험 환경에서 나타난 모기의 유인 반응이며, 실제 야외에서의 흡혈 빈도나 감염병 발생 위험을 직접 측정한 것은 아니다.

연구진은 향후 피부 미생물이 어떤 냄새 성분을 만들어 모기의 행동에 영향을 미치는지 추가로 규명할 계획이다.

The Nvidia CEO had a second affair, allegedly with an executive who reports to him, The New York Times reports.

Nvidia’s board is preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang following a report from the New York Times about a second alleged extramarital affair , just days after he admitted to a separate affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, The Wall Street Journal reports . The second alleged affair was with an executive who reports to him, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, according to the Times .

The Nvidia board will meet as soon as today to decide on Huang’s future at the company, according to the Journal . Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Verge .

Huang and Powell, who are both married to other people, were allegedly captured together at a hotel in San Jose during Nvidia’s GTC developer conference in March, two unnamed sources told the Times . The Times has not seen the video. Rumors about a potential affair between the two had long circulated at Nvidia, an unnamed source told CNBC , partially because Powell does not have a health or science background.

Nvidia’s stock fell more than 7 percent in after-hours trading Wednesday.

Since Nvidia and Huang confirmed an extramarital relationship with Megaspeed executive and alleged spy Alice Huang and a subsequent investigation over the weekend, the company has said it retained former US attorney Joon H. Kim and his firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to handle it, but today’s rumor suggests it won’t wait for those results to act. Last year, Huang hired crisis communications firm Heller known for handling public sex scandals, according to Wired . Its founder has advised several powerful men who faced public scrutiny, Wired reported, like former congressman Anthony Weiner and writer Jeffrey Toobin. Heller did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Verge .

선반 적재 성공률 73%→92%… 공항 수하물 상하차부터 적용

방송/통신 입력 :2026/11/12 07:25 수정: 2026/11/12 08:54

로봇이 짐을 옮기기 전에 짐이 떨어지거나 쌓아둔 짐이 무너질지를 먼저 따져보고, 성공 가능성이 가장 높은 동작을 골라 움직이게 하는 AI가 나왔다.

일본 NTT는 물체의 질량과 자세, 속도 같은 물리량과 운동방정식으로 로봇 행동에 따른 주변 변화를 예측하는 '월드 모델'을 개발했다고 밝혔다.

소형 로봇이 물건을 선반에 쌓는 실험에서 이 기술을 적용하자 성공률이 73.1%에서 92.3%로 19.2%포인트 높아졌다.

기존 월드 모델은 학습 데이터에 크게 의존하면서 물체끼리 부딪히는 장면을 잘못 예측했습다. 예측 영상 속에서 물체가 사라지거나 모양이 바뀌기도 했고, 학습하지 않은 상황은 제대로 내다보지 못했다.

NTT가 자체 개발한 물리 제어 어댑터는 영상에서 물체의 위치와 질량을 추정한 뒤 물리 법칙에 따라 다음 움직임을 계산한다. 이 계산을 영상 생성 모델에 반영해 로봇이 움직인 뒤 벌어질 장면을 영상으로 보여준다.

이 기술은 기존 로봇 제어 소프트웨어에 붙여 쓸 수 있다. 제어 프로그램이 내놓은 여러 동작마다 짐이 떨어지거나 부딪힐 가능성을 비교해 가장 나은 동작을 고르는 방식으로, 모양과 무게, 배치가 제각각인 화물을 다루는 현장을 겨냥했다.

NTT는 공항 수하물을 자동으로 싣고 내리는 작업에 이 기술을 먼저 적용하기로 하고 로봇 기업 무진(Mujin)과 실증을 추진한다. 이후 물류 창고를 넘어 제조, 건설, 소매 분야로 활용을 넓히고, 'NTT R&D 포럼 2026'에서 기술을 전시할 계획이다.

items.content:
기업공개(IPO)를 앞둔 앤트로픽이 투자자들을 설득하기 위해 42분짜리 영상을 공개했습니다. 다리오 아모데이 CEO를 비롯한 경영진이 직접 등장해 1조달러가 넘는 기업가치 를 인정받아야 하는 이유를 설명한 것으로, AI 안전을 강조해 온 앤트로픽이 투자자들에게 어떤 경쟁력과 성장 가능성을 내세웠는지 보여줍니다.

앤트로픽은 10일(현지시간) 투자자 대상 기업 설명회인 로드쇼(Roadshow)를 시작하고, 미국 전용 IPO 홈페이지에 설명 영상을 공개했습니다.

로드쇼는 경영진이 투자자들에게 회사를 소개하고 투자를 유치하는 행사로, 최근에는 대면 설명회와 함께 사전 제작한 영상도 활용합니다. 증권신고서가 사업 현황과 위험 요인 등을 폭넓게 공개하는 문서라면, 로드쇼는 경영진이 투자자들에게 강조하고 싶은 메시지를 직접 전달하는 자리입니다.

앤트로픽이 가장 먼저 강조한 것은 AI가 인류 역사상 가장 큰 경제적 기회를 만들 것이라는 주장입니다. 아모데이 CEO는 AI를 "인류 역사상 가장 유망한 기술"이라고 소개하며 소프트웨어 개발과 전문직 업무를 넘어 과학과 의학 연구까지 변화시킬 것으로 전망했습니다. AI가 만들어낼 시장이 워낙 크기 때문에 현재의 높은 기업가치도 정당화될 수 있다는 논리입니다.

'컴퓨팅 효율성'이라는 기술 경쟁력도 강조했습니다. 엔비디아뿐 아니라 다양한 반도체를 활용하고 알고리즘을 개선해 같은 연산 자원으로 더 뛰어난 AI를 개발할 수 있다는 주장입니다. 실제로 '미소스'를 활용해 불과 3일 만에 '클로드'를 AMD GPU에서 실행하도록 전환한 사례를 소개했습니다. 막대한 컴퓨팅 비용이 AI 기업의 가장 큰 부담인 만큼, 같은 투자로 더 많은 성과를 낼 수 있다는 점을 부각한 것입니다.

기업 시장에서 거둔 상업적 성과도 내세웠습니다. 일본 라쿠텐은 클로드를 활용해 소프트웨어 기능 출시 기간을 24일에서 5일로 단축했고, 미국 보험회사 AIG는 견적 처리 시간을 55% 줄였다고 소개했습니다. AI가 미래의 가능성에 머무르지 않고 기업들이 이미 비용을 지불하고 사용하는 생산성 도구라는 사실을 강조한 것입니다.

매출 성장과 향후 수익성도 주요 메시지였습니다. 올해 3분기 매출이 약 170억달러로 전년 동기 대비 12배 이상 증가했다고 밝혔습니다. 올해 1~3분기 누적 매출총이익률은 85%, 컴퓨팅·인프라 비용까지 반영한 이익률은 43%였으며, 장기적으로는 조정 영업이익률 35% 이상을 달성할 수 있다는 전망도 제시했습니다. AI 인프라에 막대한 자금이 필요하지만 앞으로 충분한 수익을 창출할 수 있다는 주장입니다.

특히 AI 안전을 사업 경쟁력으로 설명한 점도 주목할 만합니다. 앤트로픽은 지난 9월 공개된 IPO 관련 자료에서 AI가 인류의 생존을 위협할 가능성까지 경고해 관심을 모았습니다. 아모데이 CEO도 AI 개발 속도를 조절해야 한다고 주장하면서, 경쟁력을 유지해야 안전한 AI 개발을 주도할 수 있다는 입장 을 밝혀 왔습니다.

이번 영상에서도 아모데이는 시작 30여초 만에 AI를 이용한 생물무기 개발 위험을 언급했습니다. 그러나 발표 전반에서는 안전을 기업 고객의 신뢰와 사업 경쟁력에 연결했습니다. 앤트로픽은 안전이 기술 발전을 가로막지 않으며, 클로드의 작업을 신뢰할 수 있기 때문에 AI의 성과를 실제 업무에 적용할 수 있다고 설명했습니다. 안전을 기술 발전의 제약이 아니라 기업들이 클로드를 선택하는 이유로 제시한 것입니다.

비즈니스 인사이더 가 영상 대본을 분석한 결과도 이런 특징을 보여줍니다. '클로드'가 65회, '모델'이 58회 등장했고, 그다음으로 많이 언급된 것은 '컴퓨팅'으로 49회였습니다. '고객'은 42회, '업무'와 'AI'는 각각 39회였으며, '안전' 관련 표현은 27회였습니다. 관련 단어들을 주제별로 묶어도 모델·훈련이 83회, 컴퓨팅·인프라가 81회, 재무 성과·성장이 77회였으며, 안전·신뢰·보안·위험은 55회였습니다.

앤트로픽은 증권신고서에서 총 8950억달러에 가까운 컴퓨팅·인프라 관련 지출 약정도 공개했습니다. 로드쇼에서는 이처럼 막대한 투자 부담을 감당하면서도 성장과 수익성을 확보할 수 있다는 논리를 강조한 것으로 볼 수 있습니다. 월가에서는 앞으로 발생할 천문학적인 컴퓨팅 비용과 이에 따른 수익성 문제를 주요 투자 위험으로 지적하고 있습니다.

결국 앤트로픽이 전달하려는 메시지는 AI 시장의 성장 가능성이 막대하고, 자신들은 기술력과 컴퓨팅 효율, 기업 고객의 신뢰를 바탕으로 그 시장을 이끌 수 있다는 것입니다. 그동안 AI의 위험을 경고하는 데 앞장섰던 기업이 이제는 안전을 사업 경쟁력으로 내세우며 투자자들을 설득하고 있는 셈입니다.

■ 앤트로픽 '페이블 5.2', AI 성능 평가 1위 탈환…API 가격도 20% 인하

'클로드 페이블 5.2'가 예상대로 구글 '제미나이 4 카본'을 제치고 AI 성능 평가 1위를 되찾았습니다. 더 주목할 점은 앤트로픽이 최첨단 모델의 API 가격을 지속적으로 낮추며 성능뿐 아니라 가격 경쟁력 확보에도 적극적으로 나서고 있다는 것입니다.

■ '하이쿠' 성능에 비용은 3분의 1…메타, 에이전트용 '뮤즈 엠버' 출시

메타가 고성능 모델 '뮤즈 원더 풀'에 이어 반복적인 에이전트 작업에 특화된 저렴한 경량 모델 '뮤즈 엠버'를 출시했습니다. 복잡한 작업에는 최상위 모델을, 단순하고 반복적인 작업에는 빠르고 저렴한 모델을 사용하는 전략으로, 에이전트의 비용 효율성을 높이려는 움직임입니다.

■ 텐센트도 'AI 자기 개선' 연구 본격화…미국 이어 RSI 경쟁 가세

그동안 미국의 최첨단 AI 모델을 추격해 온 중국 AI 업계가 최근에는 AI가 스스로 성능을 높이는 '재귀적 자기 개선(RSI)' 연구에도 뛰어들고 있습니다. 텐센트가 '터미널-RSI'를 공개한 데 이어 바이두도 AI 연구를 자동화하는 '어니 이볼브'를 선보였습니다.

items.title: Pete Hegseth Is About to Get His Ass Kicked
items.summary: House Democrats are already planning to make their impeachment case against the defense secretary as airtight—and appealing to Republicans—as possible.
items.content:
It’s been one week since Election Day, and Pete Hegseth is facing a different kind of war. Trump administration officials tell Inner Loop they knew the defense secretary would face a slew of investigations in the next Congress. Now, they think he is on track to be Democrats’ number one target—and Democrats are already planning to make their case as airtight as possible.

“Hegseth is now a passenger in whatever comes next,” says one source close to President Donald Trump. “And all the outcomes are potentially damaging.”

House Democratic aides tell Inner Loop that Democrats are likely to pursue an impeachment inquiry against Hegseth, and also work to narrow the charges against him to issues that Senate Republicans have also complained about, in an effort to attract their support.

Hegseth, who has championed the deeply unpopular and costly Iran war, has spent much of his controversial tenure upending various internal processes at the Defense Department, including firing generals and blocking promotions using criteria that disproportionately affected women and people of color. He has also become known for his notorious role in Signalgate and for military strikes against purported drug traffickers in the Caribbean and Pacific Ocean.

Some of those topics have also previously been the subject of complaints from Republicans. The Senate Armed Services Committee chair Roger Wicker criticized Hegseth for the flag officer cuts and once reportedly threatened to block a Trump nominee unless the Pentagon handed over documents.

Last night, House Republicans managed to table an impeachment effort targeting Hegseth that was brought about by Representative Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky. Massie, among other issues, accused Hegseth of waging the Iran war without approval from Congress and directing “extrajudicial killings.” But even though the effort failed, officials privately believe it is practically inevitable that Hegseth will be impeached again and face a Senate trial next year.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries suggested as much after the impeachment failed to progress, telling reporters he would consult with his top members on next steps.

“We’ll have that conversation at the appropriate time, and that’ll be led by Adam Smith, soon to be chair of the Armed Services Committee, and Jamie Raskin, next chair of the judiciary,” Jeffries said.

Trump officials tell Inner Loop they still don’t expect Democrats to get enough GOP support to remove Hegseth—but they can’t shield him from wall-to-wall coverage of a trial.

The impeachment articles brought by Massie were seen by some Republicans as overly broad, which made officials think they could spare Hegseth an impeachment trial by having Senate majority leader John Thune dismiss all the charges in a straight-line vote.

But with Democrats taking over the Senate next year, that option is off the table.

It’s not going to be entirely simple, however. Hegseth’s biggest Republican detractors are all leaving Congress at the end of the year. Maine senator Susan Collins, North Carolina senator Thom Tillis, and Louisiana senator Bill Cassidy all lost reelection this midterm cycle, while Iowa senator Joni Ernst and Kentucky senator Mitch McConnell are stepping down after finishing their terms.

But even with his biggest detractors set to retire, at least five other Republican senators have complained about Hegseth’s performance—getting Democrats closer to the 67 votes needed to convict—like Wicker, South Dakota senator Mike Rounds, Kentucky senator Rand Paul, Alaska senator Lisa Murkowski, and Indiana senator Todd Young.

This is why the focus of the Democratic impeachment inquiry is going to have to be specific, and geared to Republican interests, so as to be unassailable.

Hegseth, for what it’s worth, doesn’t seem to want to go anywhere without a fight. In a televised appearance at the Pentagon earlier this week, Hegseth responded to a question about Vice President JD Vance blaming the Republican midterm losses on Iran, and said Vance was a “critical member of the team” and the war effort.

Hegseth then added, “I agree with what the president said, when he said ‘Hey, if I had to do this all over again, would we do it again? Absolutely.’”

​House Republicans are poised to open an investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's interactions with alleged Chinese spy and one-time tech executive Alice Huang, who is not related to the CEO.

The growing push for Congress to stand up its own investigation is set to put Republicans on a collision course with Trump, who has continued to publicly defend the CEO of the world's most valuable chip company.

During a congressional “Gang of Eight” briefing on Monday, officials including director of national intelligence Jay Clayton and CIA director John Ratcliffe gave only the broad brushstrokes of the classified intelligence surrounding Huang’s interactions, which left lawmakers deeply unsatisfied, sources say.

Meeting attendees did not get clear answers as to why there was no defensive briefing provided to Jensen Huang and whether he was initially left off Trump's trip to China this year as a result of the possible national security risk.

On Tuesday, the chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Brian Mast, told reporters he would be open to issuing a subpoena to compel Jensen Huang to provide a briefing behind closed doors if he ignored a request from last week to appear on Capitol Hill.

Mast, together with Rick Crawford, the chair of the House Intelligence Committee, and John Moolenaar, the chair of the China select subcommittee, had asked Jensen Huang to appear before the three panels later this month.

items.content:

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

United says it won’t let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns.

The company says it hasn’t yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book their flights, The Wall Street Journal reports , in line with observations from other businesses like Doordash . But United is concerned that agents could expose customers’ information or make purchases they didn’t intend, and potentially skirt federal rules about the kind of information airlines need to share with customers — like having them attest that their bags don’t have explosives.

While agents can still show users United flights, they won’t be able to actually complete the transaction on their behalf. The decision, and others like it, could limit the potential usefulness of newer personal AI assistants like Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots . “To be honest, I don’t want to create another middleman,” United CEO Scott Kirby said at an event on Tuesday, according to the Journal .

Across sectors, businesses are grappling with whether to let AI agents transact on their sites, and United is not alone in blocking access for unauthorized agents. eBay appeared to block agents from browsing the site, and several major banks have also placed restrictions on them. United suggests it could reconsider its decision based on future advancements. “As third-party AI agents advance, we see the opportunities they present. However, at the same time, allowing them to interact directly with a United account or booking could involve sensitive actions, and we want to make sure we have established protections for travelers first.”

items.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50458900 Points: 317 # Comments: 296
items.content:
United Airlines said on Wednesday that it is banning artificial intelligence agents from making flight reservations on behalf of travelers, citing security risks and the possibility that such actions could violate federal rules.

Many consumers are turning to AI agents such as Meta's Muse and OpenAI's dots to complete tasks ranging from researching products and tracking down deals to making purchases.

To make an airline booking, an AI agent requires access to a customer's personal information, including credentials like payment information. United has a problem with that, saying that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles."

The carrier also said that using an AI agent to, for example, check in for a flight could violate federal regulations, including rules requiring travelers to verify in person that their luggage does not contain banned substances.

"As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants," said the airline, which is updating its booking and ticketing policies to reflect the new rule.

United's new policy suggests the company wants to retain control over the customer booking process, said Henry Harteveldt, an aviation analyst at Atmosphere Research Group.

"United is saying they don't want to add yet another, and potentially even more powerful, intermediary than they already face in terms of Google search, price-comparison metasearch sites and online travel agencies," he told CBS News. "Flight searches cost airlines money, and undoubtedly United wants to avoid the expense associated with the surge of AI bot flight searches."

Other airlines are taking a different tack to the emergence of AI agents. For example, Southwest has made its flight inventory viewable to ChatGPT users, who can access the airline's website through the AI app.

United fares will continue to be bookable through flight aggregators such as Kayak, Hopper and Google Flights, Harteveldt said, adding that "consumers shouldn't find it any more difficult to find good fares on the airline."

"But by blocking the AI bots, United won't make it any easier to find its fares, either," he said.

Edited by Alain Sherter

Kris Van Cleave contributed to this report.

The data center boom is running into serious real-world obstacles, from widespread local opposition and permitting delays to a scramble for electricity . Before those challenges even come into play, though, there’s a more basic problem: A lot of the projects being announced may never get built in the first place. With billions of dollars in AI infrastructure investment at stake, separating realistic projects from speculative ones is becoming increasingly important.

items.title: Meta is losing its longtime head of infrastructure
items.summary: Santosh Janardhan, who originally joined the company in 2009, will be stepping down from his role.
items.content:
A key figure in Meta’s growth into a social media and tech industry powerhouse is leaving the company.

Santosh Janardhan, the company’s longtime head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering, will be stepping down, Meta told TechCrunch. He will be replaced by Dave Brown, who joined the company as vice president of infrastructure earlier this year, the company added. Previous to coming aboard at Meta, Brown spent 19 years at Amazon, where he focused on compute, cloud, and AI, his LinkedIn shows .

It sounds like Janardhan will remain at Meta for a little bit, although he is expected to leave next year. “Santosh will stay on for transition and he is moving into an advisory role on Meta Compute,” said a Meta representative.

Janardhan, who originally joined the company in 2009, helped the firm grow into the massive internet presence that it is today. Bloomberg originally reported Janardhan’s departure, citing an internal memo that had recently been circulated. It’s unclear why Janardhan is stepping down from the role. The memo did not specify the reasons for his departure and Meta didn’t immediately respond to a request for clarity on the issue. However, Janardhan’s memo apparently cited the need to “pass the baton.”

In recent years, the company’s investment in infrastructure has exploded , as it seeks to keep up with its competitors in the AI race. Earlier this year, Janardhan was tasked with leading Meta Compute , the company initiative to scale its data center investments and strategy.

items.title: I Saw the Future of Robotics in a Virtual Duck That Chases My Cat
items.summary: An OpenAI model helped me teach the Microduck to waddle and moonlight as a tiny cat butler.
items.content:
Allow me to introduce you to the robot cat butler I’m developing with help from AI.

Using OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol , I taught a virtual version of Microduck —a cute robot from Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face—to walk around a room and identify any bengal cats in its vicinity. (The clip above shows the robot waddling toward a target feline; its eye view is shown top right.)

I’m still waiting patiently for a physical Microduck— please hurry up and ship it, guys —but simulated behavior is relatively simple, so it should transfer over to the real thing. I plan to have the robot automatically dispense a treat for my pet bengal, Leona, perhaps by bowing its head to release one from a 3D-printed, head-mounted storage chamber.

I was able to code and train the virtual robot in just a few hours, which is, quite frankly, incredible. Previously, this kind of thing might have taken me weeks to figure out. It was possible because OpenAI’s latest models are remarkably good at understanding and manipulating 3D representations of the physical world and then translating that into useful code, agentic actions, and robot training.

Real roboticists are using the latest models to do some amazing stuff. When OpenAI released Astra this past September, University of California, Berkeley professor Ken Goldberg and his students saw demos that showcased its ability to render 3D images. They wondered if it could help with the simulations required to train different kinds of robots. These simulations need to be incredibly detailed and extremely accurate to ensure that sophisticated behavior—a humanoid that can dance or a robot hand that can grasp—will transfer faithfully to the real world.

One member of Goldberg’s lab gave Astra access to an Nvidia tool called Newton , showed it a video clip of a real robot in action, and asked if it could create a simulation of the scene.

“What blew us all away was that within an hour it had produced a full 3D simulation with all the parameters set—the position of the camera, the lighting, the background, all the materials,” Goldberg tells me.

Astra is also able to automate much of the drudgery involved with training a robot in simulation, Goldberg says, by running experiments and examining the results.

This is precisely what I found while training the virtual Microduck. Along with GPT-6 Sol, I used an agentic harness from Nous Research called Hermes and a Nvidia DGX Spark, a personal computer that contains a powerful AI chip.

I’ve previously written about using agents and coding models to configure, program, and debug physical robots. Normally, this kind of work requires significant expertise; modern coding models make it a cinch. But OpenAI’s newest model went far beyond just writing code.

It used a piece of Nvidia software called Isaac Sim to feed instructions to a model that controlled the virtual robot, watch videos of it in action to assess how well things were working, and suggest tweaks to its training regime.

This process allowed me to train the Microduck to walk around without toppling over. I initially tried getting GPT-6 Sol to teach the robot to moonwalk—I fed it a GIF of Michael Jackson sliding across the stage, which it tried to copy—but after hours of effort, it only resulted in a very jaunty backward jog. (The robots don’t have us totally beat quite yet.)

Jim Fan, a researcher at Nvidia who has collaborated with Goldberg, says the way AI can now control robots mirrors how software agents function. LLMS can use models trained to control physical actions—visual language action (VLA) models—just as they access different software on a computer.

This week, Fan, Goldberg, and others open sourced an agentic framework for robots called Aspire , which allows a robot to discover and use new skills. One example: GPT-6 Astra figured out how to use a pair of robot arms to solve a Rubik’s cube.

“It picks it up, tries to twist it, but has the wrong angle,” Fan says. “Then it reasons for a very, very long time, but it eventually is able to solve it because it learns the skills over time.”

At the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL), held in Austin, Texas, this week, Fan gave a keynote speech in which he talked about the incredible realization that AI models can automate a lot of the work needed to have a robot do sophisticated things. Fan showed off a demo in which Astra was put in control of a robot arm and told to paint a picture of the Golden Gate Bridge. Using some paint and brushes nearby, it duly completed the task .

Of course, getting robots to work reliably and efficiently is still extremely difficult, requiring significant engineering expertise. The vision system on my robot duck does not work well enough to be deployed in a real product.

Still, the ease and speed of training robots with AI could soon have an enormous impact on manufacturing and e-commerce, and Goldberg says a number of industrial robotics and automation firms have shown an interest in the approach.

items.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
items.summary: CoreWeave is increasingly asking customers to pay upfront, borrowing against specific contracts, and even looking to short-term deals that could lead to higher prices, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings.
items.content:
CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings , reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices.

The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue.

CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense.

“We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call.

Instead, CoreWeave’s plan is to rely on loans backed by specific customer contracts, drawing on funds as needed to finance most of infrastructure it still has to build to deliver on its significant backlog of $132.5 billion.

CoreWeave also said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3 billion tied to signing new customer contracts for capacity it has already built, which requires no additional spending on hardware.

Rivals Nebius and IREN have also relied on hefty Microsoft prepayments to pay for computing capacity, signaling that the industry is moving toward asking Big Tech to pay up for their buildouts.

Upfront payments could alleviate CoreWeave’s immediate borrowing needs, but they also commit the company to providing services at a price that might be less attractive down the road if compute demand continues to surge.

CoreWeave is also looking to capitalize on that growing demand by signing more shorter-term contracts that can command much higher prices.

The company raised prices across its offerings by about 25% in July and by another 10% later in the quarter. Prices are still climbing this quarter, in a way that “more than offset[s] cost increases,” said Intrator.

“We are also allocating more capacity to short-term opportunities, where the pricing justifies it, selling capacity at more than $40 million per megawatt annually, while pricing for new infrastructure on four and five-year contracts is moving to $20 million to $25 million per megawatt,” the chief executive said.

CoreWeave’s financing strategy now revolves around those opportunities. In August, the company closed a $2.6 billion loan, its first designed specifically for shorter-term customer contracts. Known as DDTL 5.5, it lets CoreWeave borrow in installments as it needs the money.

While short-term deals let CoreWeave charge higher prices and change them more frequently, it’s a tradeoff. Lenders give more weight to longer-term contracts, even if they’re priced lower, because they value predictable cash flow and consistency to repay the loan above all.

Even though Wall Street reacted positively to CoreWeave’s earnings, bond investors are much less sanguine. Last month, yields on some of the company’s bonds hit above 15%, highlighting that investors are concerned about the debt needed to fund data center buildouts before those investments see a return.

In short, CoreWeave is finding new ways to expand without relying on unsecured debt. The strategy it has chosen could boost profits, but it also carries greater risk around contract renewals and pricing — and it just goes to show how dependent the AI infrastructure boom is on sustained, and as yet unproven, demand.

TechCrunch has reached out to CoreWeave for more information about its loan facility.

items.title: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
items.summary: Fractile has now become one of the top-funded players in the race for purpose-built AI chips.
items.content:
Fractile , a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated .

Alongside the likes of Axelera , Etched , and OLIX , this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.

However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.

As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source .

Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot , its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual trade-off between memory and capacity.

This trade-off has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.

In a LinkedIn post , Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has until the end of the day Wednesday to answer a call from House Republicans for a closed-door briefing on his affair with alleged Chinese spy.
items.content:
Congress is gearing up to subpoena Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to answer their questions about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy , Bloomberg reports , citing two House Republicans.

The report comes a week after House Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent a letter to Huang asking him to appear before their committees for a joint, closed-door briefing in regards to his relations with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy.

House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that Huang has until the end of the day to respond to the request. If he doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed, said Moolenaar.

Mast, who chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee, on Wednesday said his committee is preparing a subpoena for Huang to send if he doesn’t respond.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

With zero output tokens billed, Gemini Decision 1 with the Decisions API is nearly 5x cheaper across the shared benchmark suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite with the Interactions API.

Built on Gemini’s native multimodal architecture, Gemini Decision 1 can process text, images, audio, video, and PDFs directly in a single forward pass. items.title: AWS emulator
items.summary: https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/how-autonomous-ai-agent... https://www.allthingsdistributed.com/2026/11/aws-emulator-an... Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50456631 Points: 635 # Comments: 210
items.content:
AWS Emulator is a local emulator of the AWS APIs. You use it to test your software without calling AWS, on your own machine, on a development server, or in continuous integration (CI). You don’t need an AWS account. Your requests go to the emulator, not to AWS. So you work with emulated resources instead of AWS resources. AWS Emulator has no additional service fee. You pay only for AWS resources when you deploy on AWS.

The emulator is a local program that serves an AWS API endpoint. It has no graphical interface. After you start the emulator, you set environment variables to point the AWS CLI or an AWS SDK at its endpoint. Then you run your code as usual. In embedded mode, you pass the emulator’s HTTP client to your SDK instead.

AWS Emulator is for building and testing. Don’t use it for production workloads or to test security. See Security in AWS Emulator .

Documentation: AWS Emulator User Guide

Install the aws-emulator skill, then ask your agent to set up the emulator. This needs the AWS CLI version 2.35.0 or later. See Getting started with an AI coding agent .

Point your SDK at a running emulator by setting environment variables. See Pointing your AWS SDK at AWS Emulator .

Add the emulator as a dev-dependency and run it in-process, one isolated instance per test. There is no endpoint URL, certificate, or environment variable to set. Your test wires the emulator's HTTP client straight into the SDK client. See Getting started with embedded mode , and Building from source below for its build cost.

To see how closely each service matches AWS, check the fidelity scores published with each release on the releases page . To check whether your own project is expected to work, see Checking whether your project works with AWS Emulator .

Individual gaps are tracked in the repository's issues/ directory. APIs and behaviors that don't work yet are under issues/things-that-do-not-work/ , and ones that have since been fixed move to issues/things-that-now-work/ .

You need this if you are modifying the emulator, running it from a checkout, or using embedded mode. Embedded mode compiles the emulator into your test binary, so the prerequisites and build-cost guidance below apply to it too. Most other users install a prebuilt package instead (see Quick start ). Building from source is supported on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64) ; on Windows and macOS, use the Docker path above.

The emulator serves HTTPS on 127.0.0.1:9297 (self-signed certificate).

Embedded mode compiles the emulator into your test binary, so your project's first cargo test builds the emulator's service crates alongside your own code. Budget a first build and target/ on the same order as building from source above, then fast incremental builds. Recommendation: reuse one CARGO_TARGET_DIR across projects, cache target/ (or use sccache) in CI, and pin the emulator to a release commit so it isn't rebuilt on every change.

AWS Emulator is configured to collect and report usage data to AWS, to gain insight into how AWS Emulator is used. Telemetry is on by default. AWS Emulator collects telemetry data with strict data minimization in mind, preventing identification or attribution to specific users, accounts, or organizations. Its records never include what’s in your requests or responses, your code, your credentials, or personal data. We don’t share telemetry with third parties.

For details on what is collected and how the data is handled, see Telemetry in AWS Emulator . To turn telemetry off, use one of the following options.

Start the emulator with the --telemetry option (short form -t ) set to off . This setting applies only to that emulator process.

In a container, add --telemetry off after the image name in the docker run command.

Set EMULATOR_TELEMETRY to off before you start the emulator. This setting applies to every emulator that you start from that shell.

EMULATOR_TELEMETRY accepts on , true , or 1 to turn telemetry on, and off , false , or 0 to turn it off. Values aren’t case sensitive. Any other value turns telemetry off, and the startup notice shows a warning.

To turn telemetry off for every run on a machine, add these lines to the emulator settings file, config.toml . The file is ~/.aws/emulator/config.toml on Linux and macOS, and %USERPROFILE%\.aws\emulator\config.toml on Windows. To use a different file, set the EMULATOR_CONFIG environment variable to its path.

In embedded mode, turn off telemetry in the options that you pass when you create the emulator.

You might build a tool that includes the emulator, such as a test framework that other people run. If you do, tell your users about telemetry and give them a way to turn it off. You can also ship your tool with telemetry off.

Report bugs and fidelity gaps in GitHub Issues . The most useful report names the service, the operation, your SDK and version, the request you sent, and how the response differed from real AWS. This repository does not take PRs.

items.title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
items.summary: Latest example of the AI boom’s circular financing comes as AI trade wobbles.
items.content:
Top chip manufacturer TSMC is ready to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI. That would give the Taiwanese chipmaker direct stakes in leading AI developers, even as its own contract chipmaking business has profited enormously from the AI data center buildout.

The chipmaker’s board approved plans to invest up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and another $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at the latter’s expected IPO price, according to Reuters . Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported.

But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal.

TSMC’s chip fabrication plants physically produce the vast majority of Nvidia’s chips designed for AI data center workloads and make most of Apple’s custom chips used in iPhones , Mac laptops and desktops, plus Apple’s planned AI computing server . Most of these fabs are located in Taiwan, but TSMC also operates fabs in Japan and China, and it has an expanding US manufacturing cluster in Arizona. It is also building a new fab in Germany.

Meanwhile, Anthropic and OpenAI are both purchasing huge quantities of AI hardware manufactured by TSMC for their data center projects. So TSMC’s announced investment certainly seems to fit into the broader trend of circular financing that has become common during the AI boom, even as tech stocks have gyrated recently as investors have grown increasingly jittery.

Still, TSMC has plenty of money to spare on such a bet. Ongoing demand for AI-related chips has enabled the Taiwanese chipmaker to report six consecutive quarters of record profit, with the latest example being the company earning more than $23 billion in profit during the July through September 2026 quarter, according to Reuters .

TSMC’s planned investment in Anthropic and OpenAI also pales in comparison with circular financing deals from major US tech companies. The most notable example is Nvidia , which has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and $10 billion in Anthropic so far, in addition to putting tens of billions of dollars into many other AI and robotics companies .

items.summary: Gaming, social media, and e-commerce platforms are facing a fresh wave of sweeping European Union rules that aim to make "your online experience fairer." The newly proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA) published by the EU Commission on Wednesday is designed to tackle practices that
items.content:
The proposed Digital Fairness Act seeks to bolster consumer protections for online users.﻿

Gaming, social media, and e-commerce platforms are facing a fresh wave of sweeping European Union rules that aim to make “your online experience fairer.” The newly proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA) published by the EU Commission on Wednesday is designed to tackle practices that exploit consumers into spending more of their time and money online, including misleading prices or availability, addictive design features like gaming loot boxes, undisclosed influencer marketing, and more.

“The Act will protect consumers of all ages shopping and browsing for goods or services online,” the EU Commission said in a news bulletin . “It will also mean fairer competition for businesses, which are expecting to save EU consumers up to €13.7 billion ($15.1 billion) a year.”

Here’s an overview of what the DFA proposal includes:

The scope of the restrictions being proposed is broad, and could have a significant impact on major parts of the online digital landscape, from the “rabbit hole” algorithms across YouTube, TikTok, and Meta platforms, to AI chatbots and apps like DuoLingo that relentlessly nudge users to keep interacting with them. Some gaming organizations have already slammed the DFA proposal , describing its restrictions around virtual currencies, loot boxes, and offering micro-transactions to minors as being “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate.”

Given this is a draft proposal, the DFA will undergo various approvals through the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union before being passed into law, and its current measures could be changed or removed entirely as part of that process. When (or if) it does come into force, the EU Commission says companies who violate the regulations could see fines of up to six percent of their worldwide annual turnover.

“Our consumer protection rules will help ensure that businesses compete on the merits of their products and services - not on their ability to exploit consumers or evade the rules. We are not making it harder to do business. We are making it harder to do business unfairly,” EU Commissioner Michael McGrath said in remarks following the DFA draft publication. “We cannot have 21st-century consumers protected by rules that have not kept pace with the 21st-century economy.”

items.title: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
items.summary: Any amount of AI coding is too much for many Independent Games Festival judges.
items.content:
The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players. That debate has exploded into a full-blown controversy in the indie game development space this week, as Big Walk developer House House has publicly and belatedly disclosed minimal AI use in its popular co-operative puzzle exploration game.

This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. But the debate started to break into public view on Monday when 19 members of the 50-plus-member jury released a signed statement outlining a stance “declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity.”

Noting “a significant increase in the number of submitted games developer with generative AI tools,” the group of jurors called out AI’s ecological, economic, psychological, and labor harms in rejecting tools whose use, they said, is still “not a foregone conclusion in our industry.”

The jurors also urged the IGF as a whole to “adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work.”

Although the jurors’ statement didn’t name any specific games, by Tuesday morning, one critical darling in particular was increasingly being noted as a central part of the debate. In a statement provided to Aftermath (and added to the game’s FAQ page shortly thereafter), developer House House admitted publicly that “LLMs were used sparingly” near the end of Big Walk ‘s development “to help work through some difficult technical challenges and bugs.”

That limited AI use—which House House says represents “well under 0.1% of Big Walk ‘s code—stemmed in part from a thorny Unity engine bug that was slowing the game down with “infinite length” shadows during some game situations. After consulting with a Unity engineer who determined a fix “wasn’t possible,” House House said it consulted an LLM chatbot, which suggested a possible fix that the developers “had to modify… extensively” into the 10 lines of code that ended up in the final game ( At least one social media user says the bug was indeed fixable with significant human effort, though).

House House said it didn’t disclose this LLM usage for Big Walk ‘s Steam release earlier this year because Valve “does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage.” Indeed, Valve’s AI disclosure form for developers specifically notes that it is concerned with AI-generated content, not “efficiency gains” from “modern game development environments [that] have AI powered tools built into them.”

The IGF Awards make no such distinction for AI usage, however, which led House House to mention its AI-assisted bug fix in submitting the game for awards consideration. A version of that disclosure is being made public now because “it has become a matter of public interest,” House House said.

“This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal,” House House wrote. “We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalization of this technology, or its treatment as ‘inevitable.’ We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologize that Big Walk ’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.”

Learning of House House’s AI disclosure was particularly painful for some IGF judges who had previously felt a special connection to Big Walk . In a blog post discussing his feelings , IGF jurist Austin Walker called the game “an achievement” that was “remarkable” and “beautiful,” featuring puzzles that “capture a range of play that is largely abandoned by the digital form.” Fellow jurist Damon Reece shared in a blog post that the game is “seriously special to me” and that it gave him “a profound and powerful emotional reaction to being in a space that felt like home.”

But when it comes to IGF awards consideration, Walker and Reece were among those who said that even minimal use of AI tools overrode that deep and abiding respect for the work itself.

“We have our hands on the lever here,” Reece wrote. “This is pain that has to happen [emphasis in original] to try and steer our culture away from this. We need to choose to speak loudly and clearly on this, to prioritize human creativity and labour, to tell the culture and the world that this is unacceptable to us. To do otherwise is rank cowardice.”

This isn’t the first time AI usage has noticeably affected game award judging. Last year, the Indie Game Awards (which are completely separate from the IGF Awards) rescinded awards for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 after the developers admitted that some in-game textures were made using AI tools (these were later patched out).

“The Indie Game Awards have a hard stance on the use of gen AI throughout the nomination process and during the ceremony itself,” they said at the time.

Since House House’s public disclosure, the anti-AI contingent of IGF judges has found plenty of support from disappointed Big Walk fans and industry observers. In the last few days, the game’s Steam page has been bombed with over 400 negative reviews, though Steam’s anti-review-bomb tools seem to be limiting the impact on the game’s overall “Very Positive” reception there.

But others feel House House’s relatively minimal use of AI here is being blown out of proportion. They say it’s important to differentiate between games that use LLMs as a last-resort technical fix, for instance, and others that lean heavily on AI to generate the bulk of their art, music, or the core of the game engine itself.

수상자 다섯 명은 시상식에 직접 참석해 라인하르트 겐첼(Reinhard Genzel) 심사위원장으로부터 금메달과 상장을 받았다. 천문학 부문 수상자인 노모토 겐이치(Ken'ichi Nomoto) 교수와 스탠퍼드 우슬리(Stanford Woosley) 교수는 사전 녹화 영상으로 소감을 전했다. 노모토 교수는 자신의 초신성 연구를 돌아보며 국제 협력의 중요성을 강조했다. 우슬리 교수는 개략적이고 정성적인 이론을 예측이 가능한 정밀한 모델로 발전시킨 과정을 설명하고, 스승과 공동 연구자들에게 감사를 표했다.

급성 전골수구성 백혈병 치료의 발전 과정을 돌아본 생명과학•의학 부문 수상자들의 소감에서도 협력의 중요성이 핵심을 이뤘다. 안 드장(Anne Dejean) 교수는 프랑스와 중국 간 수십 년에 걸친 과학 교류를 바탕으로 이어진 기초연구와 임상 현장의 대화를 강조했다. 국제 협력은 위그 드 테(Hugues de Thé) 교수의 예에서도 확인됐다. 상호 존중과 신뢰, 지속성을 바탕으로 천주(Zhu Chen) 교수와 30년 넘게 교류를 이어왔기 때문이다. 천 교수는 이들의 성공을 '동서양의 만남(East meets West)'이라고 표현하면서 의학 발전을 뒷받침하는 집단 지성을 강조하고, 다른 혈액암에 맞서기 위한 국제 협력을 강화하겠다고 밝혔다.

수리과학 부문 수상자들은 AI의 변화하는 역할과 영향력을 탐구했다. 에마뉘엘 캉데스(Emmanuel Candès) 교수는 AI를 더욱 강력하고 안전하게 만들려는 현재의 노력을 비롯해 수학의 영역을 넘어선 질문들이 자신의 연구에 어떻게 영감을 줬는지 설명했다. 카밀로 데 렐리스(Camillo De Lellis) 교수는 젊은 수학자들에게 AI를 인간의 창의성을 대체하는 수단이 아니라 창의성을 발휘하도록 돕는 도구로 받아들일 것을 당부했다.

이 같은 미래 지향적 관점은 지난 1월 발표된 신설 컴퓨터과학 부문에도 반영돼 있다. 이 상은 컴퓨터과학 분야의 지적 깊이와 과학적 발견, 사회 변혁에 기여한 인물에게 수여된다. 케네스 영(Kenneth Young) 쇼상 평의회 의장은 "이는 과학이 계속 발전하고 성장하는 상황에서 탁월한 업적을 기리겠다는 쇼상의 의지를 재확인하는 것이기도 하다"고 말했다. 네 부문 모두 후보 추천을 11월 30일까지 받는다. 컴퓨터과학 부문의 첫 수상자를 포함해 2027년 수상자는 2027년 5월 또는 6월 발표될 예정이다.

쇼상은 인류에 긍정적이고 심대한 영향을 끼친 업적을 이룬 인물을 기리고자 런런 쇼(Run Run Shaw)의 후원으로 2002년 제정됐으며, 2004년 처음 시상됐다. 2027년부터는 천문학, 컴퓨터과학, 생명과학•의학, 수리과학, 이렇게 네 부문에서 매년 시상한다. 부문별 상금은 미화 120만 달러다. 올해로 시상 23회째를 맞았다.

이 기사는 번역본이며, 전문적인 정확성을 위해 영문 버전을 참고하시기 바랍니다.

items.title: Apple is shuttering its 28-year-old online community forum
items.summary: Apple has already made the forum read-only.
items.content:
Apple’s online community forum will close on November 20.

On Tuesday night, Apple posted a message to the Apple Support Community announcing the forum’s closure:

The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state.

You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site .

We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products.

For 28 years, the forum has provided Apple users with a way to get quick technical advice about their products. That advice usually came from fellow users, though Apple employees occasionally chimed in. As with any community forum, the helpfulness and accuracy of the advice varied.

Apple reportedly told MacRumors that it is shutting down the forum after evaluating its support strategy and customer needs.

The Apple Support Community dates to 1998, when the online forum was known as Apple Tech Exchange. Two years later, Apple renamed the community forum to Apple Discussions. In 2011 , Apple revamped the forum, adding dedicated communities for specific devices and the ability to track responses to posted questions, while renaming it Apple Support Communities. By 2022, the forum was called Apple Support Community, as MacRumors noted this week.

Based on yesterday’s announcement, it seems Apple now prefers that its customers rely on official Apple employees for technical support. The forum may also have become less popular as rival forums grow, including Reddit and the technical support communities on the MacRumors and AppleInsider forums.

items.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons With AI
items.summary: Radical Numerics has developed a model that it says can identify natural and AI-engineered pathogens without an internet connection.
items.content:
Frontier AI labs have warned that their technology could help develop dangerous bioweapons .

Now, a startup says it has developed a defense. On Wednesday, Radical Numerics announced that it has developed a new edge model called Omnii Defense that is designed to flag natural and AI-engineered pathogens using a laptop and a USB gene sequencer. It can also run without an internet connection, allowing researchers in the field with spotty connections to use it. Though many scientists say AI-made bioweapons are a low-likelihood threat, Radical Numerics hopes its technology will help researchers and public health officials identify emerging biological threats.

Eric Nguyen, cofounder and CEO of Radical Numerics, says he sees a coming arms race in biodefense similar to what’s playing out in cybersecurity , where threat actors and security defenders are leveraging AI in an attempt to gain an edge.

“We felt that the biosecurity space was far behind on the defense side,” he says.

Nguyen and his cofounders were part of the research team behind Evo and Evo-2, open-source DNA foundation models they worked on during their doctoral research at Stanford University. They founded Radical Numerics in 2025.

The San Francisco–based company recently made waves after rolling out Omnii, a new genome language model built on different types of biological information beyond DNA, including RNA, proteins, and epigenetic signals. In October, Radical announced that it used Omnii to create custom bacteriophages , viruses that infect and kill specific bacteria, targeting a drug-resistant strain of E. coli. Its cocktail was used to treat a sick patient, with special permission from the Food and Drug Administration.

Another AI biotech startup, Tabula Bioscience, was also involved in that research, but Radical didn’t disclose the partnership in its announcement last month. The omission led Harvard geneticist George Church, who was an adviser to both companies, to resign from his role at Radical last week.

Omnii Defense, the company’s latest tool, makes multiple predictions about a sequence, including the odds of it being pathogenic or AI-generated and what taxonomic group it most closely resembles. The model assigns a genome a “threat score” between zero and one that combines the likelihood of unnaturalness with functional predictions. The higher the score, the higher the threat.

Earlier biodefense tools, such as the federally funded Finding Engineering-Linked Indicators, or Felix, can compare genetic sequences of interest against libraries of known organisms, essentially searching for cataloged matches. That can be helpful in a scenario where a bad actor has made a few tweaks to an existing pathogen. But they aren’t designed to make predictions in the way that Omnii is.

The benefit of AI models is that they can learn patterns in sequences associated with biological function instead of relying on exact sequence matches. That could allow them to recognize similarities between sequences even when their genetic spelling has changed. Christine Parthemore, Radical Numerics’ head of biodefense, says Omnii is a “step change.”

In one experiment, the company removed Bundibugyo virus—which is currently driving an Ebola outbreak in East Africa —from the training data, first at the species level and then its whole genus. “It was as if Omnii was operating in 1976,” Parthemore says, referring to the year Ebola was discovered. With just the species removed, the model still detected that 33 percent of the Bundibugyo sequences pushed to it were something pathogenic. Even with the whole genus removed, it flagged 22 percent of the viral sequences. Non-AI tools gave essentially no indication of potential risk, she says.

“We absolutely need to be vigilant about what AI is enabling, and if we can use technology to compete with it and hopefully get ahead of any kind of nefarious actors, that seems sensible,” says Bronwyn MacInnis, director of pathogen surveillance in the Infectious Disease and Microbiome program at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard.

However, MacInnis cautions that detecting a signal is still a big leap from determining whether a pathogen has real consequence or whether a threat was engineered.

Access to Omnii Defense is currently limited to vetted external testers. Radical Numerics says it is working with national laboratories, government agencies, and other independent evaluators to assess the model’s performance.
